_doc: The 1871 city's street furniture (owner, 2026-11-21): gas lamps, telegraph poles and wires, and hitching posts. GENERATED by tools/lay_1871_street_furniture.py from data/context/1871.json -- do not hand-edit; re-run the tool. Local ENU metres of data/datum.json; heading_deg is the compass bearing of the street the item stands along; y_m is the walk's own height, which every item stands on. Drawn by renderers/web/js/street-furniture.js. docs/LIBERTIES.md L-1871-streetscape.

gas_lamp.name: gas street lamp
gas_lamp.form: A cast-iron post: a plain round foot on a plinth, a moulded collar, a leafed boss at knee height, a slender shaft, a bell capital under a knobbed ladder bar, four scrolled arms bent up into the foot of a clear four-sided lantern that tapers out to an iron waist band, a steep glazed top on iron hips, a small cap, vent and knob; painted iron. About 3.1 m. The Glessner corner's lamp stands on a stone pad level with the walk.
gas_lamp.form_note: Carbutt's stereographs of Lake and Dearborn, Washington Street and Clark and Randolph show cast-iron posts with a four-sided glazed lantern at the corners and before the opera house's door, about the height of a man and a half. Every 1871 lamp is drawn with the 1904 layer's post (data/street_furniture/1904.json, read off the 1880s Prairie Avenue photographs), the same pattern of post and lantern; its mouldings are not read off the 1860s pictures.
gas_lamp.rule_note: The 1860s stereographs show gas lamps at the corners of the business streets and before their doors

utility_pole.name: telegraph pole
utility_pole.form: A wooden pole about 12 m, tapering from its butt, with five crossarms of six pins and glass insulators.
utility_pole.form_note: Carbutt's No. 52 shows the Clark Street poles at the kerb with five or six crossarms and the wires running down the street; No. 55 a tall pole with short crossarms at Lake and Dearborn. Every pole is drawn alike.
utility_pole.what: A wooden pole carrying the telegraph lines
utility_pole.rule_note: The 1860s stereographs show telegraph poles at the kerb of the principal business streets

hitching_post.name: hitching post
hitching_post.form: A cast-iron post about 1.1 m, a ring at its head to tie a horse's rein to, on the walk at the kerb.
hitching_post.form_note: Carbutt's No. 139 shows a horse and buggy standing at the Washington Street kerb; the posts they were tied to are too small in any of the pictures to read, so the post is the plain iron kind of the period, reconstructed.
hitching_post.what: A post to tie a horse to
hitching_post.rule_note: Horses stand at the kerb in every picture of the business streets

gas_lamp.note: A lamp at each corner of the platted city's named streets, on the walk 0.45 m in from the kerb and 1.2 m back from the corner; on the business streets one about every 46 m between, the two sides staggered. Reconstructed.

utility_pole.note: On one side of each principal business street where it fronts shops, about every 40 m, 0.3 m in from the kerb; wires join neighbouring poles. Reconstructed.

hitching_post.note: Along the walks that front shop rows, about every 7.5 m at the kerb, clear of the lamps and poles. Reconstructed.

loc_stereo_1s12371_sherman_house.citation: John Carbutt, '52.—Sherman House, cor. Clark and Randolph Streets', stereograph, Stereographs of Chicago (Chicago: J. Carbutt, 131 Lake Street, [1860s]). Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LC-DIG-stereo-1s12371.
loc_stereo_1s12371_sherman_house.date: [between 1861 and 1871] (the Library dates it between 1860 and 1930; the building it shows stood from July 1861 to October 1871)

loc_stereo_1s47902_crosbys_opera_house.citation: John Carbutt, '139.—Crosby's Opera House, Washington Street', stereograph (Chicago: J. Carbutt, 131 Lake Street, [between ca. 1860 and 1870]). Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LC-DIG-stereo-1s47902.
loc_stereo_1s47902_crosbys_opera_house.date: [between ca. 1865 and 1870] (the Library dates the card between ca. 1860 and 1870; the opera house opened in April 1865)
